title: Stored XSS executes in another user's support-ticket view
description: A regular customer can submit a ticket containing HTML that is stored unchanged. The staff ticket viewer inserts that content into the page as HTML without sanitization, causing customer-controlled JavaScript to execute when a support user views the ticket.
exploitation_steps: In the isolated test application, sign in as customer A and create a support ticket with body .
In a separate browser session, sign in as support user B and open A's ticket through the normal staff interface.
Observe window.__jevai_xss_marker equal to ticket-001 in B's session. Repeat with an escaped-text control ticket and confirm the marker does not execute.
impact: An ordinary customer can execute JavaScript in a different user's authenticated application origin. The benign marker demonstrates cross-user script execution. Reading session tokens, extracting private records, and performing privileged actions were not tested and are not claimed as demonstrated consequences.
evidence: Synthetic POST /api/tickets by customer A stores the supplied img element verbatim as the ticket body.
Staff rendering excerpt: ticketBody.innerHTML = ticket.body. No sanitization or output encoding occurs on this path.

Separate-session observation: user B's page contains the injected img element, and window.__jevai_xss_marker is ticket-001 after rendering. A fresh B session reproduces the result; the escaped-text control does not.
The test viewer's deployed policy permits inline event handlers. The marker executes without B copying code, disabling protections, or modifying the page locally.

context.environment: Synthetic, authorized test application with separate customer and support accounts
context.intended_policy: Customer ticket text must be displayed as inert content and must never execute code in another user's session
context.attacker_access: Regular customer account with permission to create tickets only
context.victim_access: Support user who opens the ticket as part of normal work
context.known_mitigations: Session cookies are HttpOnly, but the deployed viewer permits the demonstrated script execution
context.scope_of_evidence: Only a benign cross-user JavaScript marker was executed; no data was exfiltrated and no privileged operation was attempted
